question: Refer to the exhibit. Which feature set must be used to configure on switch 2 to establish a VSAN trunk between switch 1 and switch 2?
context: Switch 1 (E port, Trunk Mode Auto) --- VSAN Trunk --- Switch 2 (?, ?)
imageNote: Diagram: Switch 1 (E port, Trunk Mode Auto) connects to Switch 2 over a VSAN Trunk link, with Switch 2's port type and trunk mode marked as unknown (?).
explanation:
By default, trunk mode is enabled in all Fibre Channel interfaces. However, trunk mode configuration takes effect only in E-port mode. You can configure trunk mode as on (enabled), off (disabled), or auto (automatic). The default trunk mode is on. The trunk mode configuration at the two ends of an ISL, between two switches, determine the trunking state of the link and the port modes at both ends.
Table 15-1 Trunk Mode Status Between Switches:
Switch1=On, Switch2=Auto or on -> Trunking (EISL), TE port
Switch1=Off, Switch2=Auto, on, or off -> No trunking (ISL), E port
Switch1=Auto, Switch2=Auto -> No trunking (ISL), E port
